description: We have a multi-skilled group, each member being well versed in different areas, such as linguistics, psychology and technology. Our project consists of a visual novel game, destined to the youth. We look for people who can contribute by bringing new knowledge!
summary:
Humans have left nearly 200 tonnes of hardware on the Moon and more than 7,000 kg on Mars. 

Almost none of it has a public face.  Space High is a browser-based visual novel in which every student is a real piece of equipment humanity left behind. The player arrives at a school on Mars carrying a helmet with ten dark lamps, one per classmate, and lights them by learning each machine's story. 

NASA data did two jobs here. First, it built the characters: every personality is derived from the mission record, not invented. Ingenuity was built for five flights and made seventy-two, so he brags. Viking asked the biggest question in planetary exploration, got an ambiguous answer, and was silenced by a mistyped command, so he is the perfectionist who cannot let it go. Through the story the player not only will get to know the characters but can also play mini games and quizzes related to its contents.  

Second, the same data is what the characters teach. Every factual claim has a sourced entry in the in-game Archive, next to the real NASA photograph of that machine.  The challenge calls this equipment abandoned but not forgotten. 

We gave ten of them a voice.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Space High is a visual novel that runs in any browser. The player is a new student at a school on Mars where every classmate is a real piece of equipment left behind on the Moon or Mars.

A clickable map spans two worlds. Each character lives in a fixed location, and the player travels between them. Talking to a character raises a friendship level from 1 to 5, and each level unlocks denser material: first the main chapters, then a personal chapter, then a special one. A short quiz closes each chapter.

An in-game Archive holds a technical file on every machine at three levels of depth, each with its source and the real NASA photograph of that hardware.

The helmet the player carries from the prologue has ten dark lamps, one per machine. Finishing a machine's story lights its lamp. Ten of ten ends the game.

Until now, he project contains 47 scenes across 16 locations, around 400 lines of dialogue, and 10 machines spanning 60 years of exploration, from Surveyor in 1966 to Ingenuity in 2021.



HOW WE USED NASA DATA

Two ways, and this is the core of the project.

First, as character construction. Each personality was derived from the mission record rather than invented. Opportunity was guaranteed 90 Martian days and worked for fourteen years, covering 45 km, so she speaks in short declaratives and never boasts. Ingenuity was built for five test flights and made seventy-two, so the gap between what was promised and what was delivered is literally his personality. Viking 1 carried three biology experiments, received ambiguous results, and was silenced in 1982 by a mistyped command, so he is the perfectionist who cannot let an unresolved answer go. The retroreflector has no electronics to fail and has been answering since 1969, so he deals only in measurement.

Second, as the content the characters teach. A player does not read about the retroreflector; they talk to it, and it explains why the Moon recedes 3.8 cm per year while telling them why it never stopped working. Teaching stops being an interruption and becomes the conversation.

Every factual claim is checkable. The Archive carries the source for each one.




INTENDED IMPACT

The challenge frames this hardware as abandoned but not forgotten. Researchers who have catalogued the debris make the same argument: what matters about it is its place in history, because these machines are the early milestones of planetary exploration.

A list of 18 objects across 14 missions is a dataset. A classmate who tells you he was built for five flights and made seventy-two is a memory.

The project turns the first into the second without giving up a single fact.

It is free, opens from a link, needs no installation or account, and runs offline once loaded. Its main focus is to make this knowledge more accessible and interesting for younger generations; it was made with the intention to reach people aged 12 and up by translating the missions dense content into an easier language.


TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, written by hand. No framework, no build step, no runtime dependency, no server. The game is one static file plus an art folder, so it opens by double-click or from a public link and keeps working with no network.

Typography uses Google Fonts. Automated playthrough tests run in jsdom and verify the full path end to end: prologue, every location, the map switch, the storm, the branching routes, and the finale with ten of ten lamps lit, with no console errors.

AI tools assisted with illustration, code and text. See the SI declaration.


WHY IT IS CREATIVE

The friendship-based visual novel is a format built to make players care about characters. We pointed it at machines that no one grieves for.

Friendship as progression is the mechanic that carries the teaching: depth is earned, not dumped. The deepest material only exists for a player who came back.

And one character never speaks. Spirit is present through absence: a closed door in the dormitory, and the story her twin tells about her. Her lamp lights with her sister's.


WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Accuracy first. Every claim is sourced in the Archive, and we deliberately avoided the myths that circulate about these machines. Opportunity never said her battery was low; that was a journalist's poetic reading of a status report. Viking did not confirm life; the results were ambiguous and remain disputed. Only the descent stage of the lunar module stayed on the Moon.

Every photograph of a real machine is an actual NASA image in the public domain, downloaded from NASA sources and credited. Inventing an original picture of a real spacecraft in a project judged on accuracy would undo the rest of the work.

Accessibility and reach. Map indicators differ by shape and not only by colour. The script is structured for translation into English and Spanish alongside Portuguese.
